expectation: Membrane rings on scattered single NK cells and a subset of CD8 T cells. These are a small minority of all cells, sitting in the lamina propria and stroma or among infiltrating lymphocytes, and occasionally between epithelial cells. Epithelium and stroma should be negative.
observed: A: the whole mucosa is bright and follows the tissue outline and crypt architecture; the muscle layer is dimmer. B and C: diffuse cytoplasmic signal fills the epithelium and lamina propria, with no distinct cells. D: haze over all cells alike, with no clear membrane-ringed subset.
why: The signal follows tissue density and epithelial cytoplasm everywhere rather than marking a sparse population of membrane-ringed lymphocytes.
notes: NKG2A lights the whole mucosa (epithelium and lamina propria) as diffuse haze that tracks the tissue's architecture. No separate population of scattered membrane-ringed NK or CD8 cells shows at any scale.
